rows.stem: In the given figure, PT is tangent to a circle with centre O. Chord PQ subtends an angle of \(65^\circ\) at the centre. The measure of \(\angle QPT\) is :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - which side of P the point T lies on (T is on the tangent below P, on the same side as Q, so the angle QPT takes in the minor arc PQ) is shown only in the drawing; the 65 degree angle at O between OQ and OP is also marked. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
\(OP = OQ\) (radii), so triangle OPQ is isosceles and \(\angle OPQ = \angle OQP = \dfrac{180^\circ - 65^\circ}{2} = 57.5^\circ\).

PT is a tangent, so \(OP \perp PT\) and \(\angle OPT = 90^\circ\). Then \(\angle QPT = 90^\circ - 57.5^\circ = 32.5^\circ\), half the angle the chord subtends at the centre.

This is option (D) \(32.5^\circ\).

rows.subtopic: Solving a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
rows.stem: Value of k for which \(x = 2\) is a solution of the equation \(5x^2 - 4x + (2 + k) = 0\), is
rows.solution:
\(x = 2\) satisfies the equation, so \(5(2)^2 - 4(2) + (2 + k) = 0\), that is \(20 - 8 + 2 + k = 0\).

So \(14 + k = 0\) and \(k = -14\), which is option (D) \(-14\).

rows.subtopic: Section Formula and Ratio of Division
rows.stem: The vertices of a \(\Delta ABC\) are \(A(-2, 4)\), \(B(4, 3)\) and \(C(1, -6)\). Find length of the median BD.
rows.solution:
The median BD joins B to the mid-point D of AC: \(D = \left(\dfrac{-2 + 1}{2}, \dfrac{4 - 6}{2}\right) = \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}, -1\right)\).

\(BD = \sqrt{\left(4 + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 + (3 + 1)^2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{81}{4} + 16} = \sqrt{\dfrac{145}{4}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{145}}{2}\) units.

rows.subtopic: Solving a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
rows.stem: Three consecutive integers are such that sum of the square of second and product of other two is 161. Find the three integers.

rows.solution:
Write the left side as a sum of cubes and use \(a^3 + b^3 = (a + b)(a^2 + b^2 - ab)\):

LHS \(= (\sin^2\theta)^3 + (\cos^2\theta)^3 = (\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta)\left[\sin^4\theta + \cos^4\theta - \sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta\right]\)

\(= \sin^4\theta + \cos^4\theta - \sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta\), since \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\).

Now \(\sin^4\theta + \cos^4\theta = (\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta)^2 - 2\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta\), so

LHS \(= 1 - 2\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta = 1 - 3\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta =\) RHS.

rows.stem: The angle of elevation of an aircraft from a point A on the ground is \(60^\circ\). After a flight of 30 seconds, the angle of elevation changes to \(30^\circ\). The aircraft is flying at a constant height of \(3500\sqrt{3}\) m at a uniform speed. Find the speed of the aircraft.
rows.solution:
Let P and Q be the positions of the aircraft at the two sightings, and B and C the points on the ground directly below them, so \(PB = QC = 3500\sqrt{3}\) m. Let \(AB = x\) m and \(BC = y\) m; the aircraft flies at a constant height, so the distance it covers in 30 seconds is \(PQ = BC = y\). The angles of elevation are \(\angle PAB = 60^\circ\) and \(\angle QAC = 30^\circ\).

In right triangle PBA: \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{3500\sqrt{3}}{x} = \sqrt{3}\), so \(x = 3500\) m ... (i)

In right triangle QCA: \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{3500\sqrt{3}}{x + y} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\), so \(x + y = 3500 \times 3 = 10500\) m.

Using (i), \(y = 10500 - 3500 = 7000\) m.

Speed of the aircraft \(= \dfrac{7000}{30} = \dfrac{700}{3}\) m/s, about 233.3 m/s (that is, 840 km/h).

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.stem: If the length of a rectangle is reduced by 5 cm and its breadth is increased by 2 cm, then the area of the rectangle is reduced by \(80\,\text{cm}^2\). However, if we increase the length by 10 cm and decrease the breadth by 5 cm, its area is increased by \(50\,\text{cm}^2\). Find the length and breadth of the rectangle.
rows.solution:
Let the length of the rectangle be x cm and its breadth y cm, so its area is \(xy\).

First condition: \((x - 5)(y + 2) = xy - 80\), that is \(2x - 5y - 10 = -80\), or \(2x - 5y + 70 = 0\) ... (1)

Second condition: \((x + 10)(y - 5) = xy + 50\), that is \(-5x + 10y - 50 = 50\), or \(x - 2y + 20 = 0\) ... (2)

From (2), \(x = 2y - 20\). Substituting in (1): \(2(2y - 20) - 5y + 70 = 0\), so \(-y + 30 = 0\) and \(y = 30\). Then \(x = 60 - 20 = 40\).

Check: \(35 \times 32 = 1120 = 1200 - 80\) and \(50 \times 25 = 1250 = 1200 + 50\).

The length of the rectangle is 40 cm and its breadth is 30 cm.
